title: ABBV Stock Gains On Winning FDA Approval For Rare Blood Cancer Drug - Stocktwits
content: AbbVie (ABBV) share price gained on Wednesday after U.S. Federal health regulators approved the company’s drug tailored to combat an ultra-rare, aggressive form of blood cancer. The Food and Drug Administration announced its approval of pivekimab sunirine-pvzy (sold under the brand name Decnupaz, made by AbbVie) on Wednesday. The drug is classified as an antibody-drug conjugate (a targeted therapy that pairs a cancer-seeking antibody with a potent cell-killing drug), specifically designed to bind to a protein commonly found on these cancer cells. The FDA based its decision on data from an open-label (a study where both doctors and participants know which treatment is being given), single-arm clinical trial known as CADENZA. The study tracked both newly diagnosed patients and those with recurrent cancer. Among 33 patients who were treatment-naïve (patients who have never received any previous medical treatment for their illness), the results were highly encouraging. Roughly 69.7% of these individuals achieved a complete remission or a clinical complete remission (a state where tumors shrink completely and blood counts normalize, even if minor skin lesions remain). For these patients, the response lasted an average of 9.7 months. The drug also showed measurable, though lower, activity in patients with relapsed or refractory (cancer that has returned or stopped responding to prior treatments) forms of the disease. In that group of 51 patients, 15.7% achieved a complete remission, lasting an average of 9.2 months. The FDA required the medication to feature a Boxed Warning—the agency's most prominent safety alert—warning doctors and patients about the potential for severe hepatotoxicity (liver damage). Specifically, the treatment can trigger hepatic veno-occlusive disease (a rare, life-threatening condition where the small blood vessels inside the liver become blocked and inflamed). Uber Technologies Inc. (UBER) share price gained nearly 1% on Wednesday amid media reports the company is considering a higher acquisition offer for German food delivery giant Delivery Hero after a major shareholder rebuffed a recent multibillion-dollar proposal. The San Francisco-based tech company acquired Aspex Management’s 14.6% stake in Delivery Hero earlier this week through a series of share purchases and derivatives, Financial Times reported citing three people familiar with the matter. Uber agreed to pay slightly below €40 per share, valuing Berlin’s Delivery Hero at about €12bn, the people added. The Berlin-based delivery company confirmed that Uber initially submitted an indicative proposal of €33 per share, a bid valuing the entire company at approximately €10 billion ($11.6 billion). Following that opening approach, Uber Chief Executive Dara Khosrowshahi traveled to Oslo to present the parameters of the deal to Kristin Skogen Lund, the chair of Delivery Hero's supervisory board. However, when Uber later extended a sweeter offer of 38 euros per share directly to one of Delivery Hero's largest investors, the proposal was rejected, the Financial Times reported. In response to the pushback, the Uber board of directors held a weekend meeting to discuss the status of the takeover bid and determine whether to increase the offer price again, according to sources familiar with the matter. Uber’s delivery platform rival DoorDash Inc. has also been circling the German firm. DoorDash has held exploratory inquiries with Delivery Hero shareholders, though it has not yet acquired any direct equity, the Financial Times noted. Uber is already deeply embedded in Delivery Hero's equity structure. Earlier this month, the ride-hailing and delivery pioneer rapidly expanded its holding to a 19.5% direct stake, supplemented by financial derivatives representing an additional 5.6%. On Tuesday, Verra Mobility stated it received a termination notice from Avis Budget regarding their contract, effective September 2026. As a result, the company is cutting costs and reallocating resources tied to Avis to other customers.The termination is expected to reduce Commercial Services' 2026 annualized revenue by about $135 million to $145 million and segment profit by $120 million to $125 million, before cost reduction initiatives. Bitwise's Hyperliquid ETF (BHYP) pulled in roughly $19 million in a single day on Tuesday, marking its largest daily inflow to date and pushing the fund past its rival to become the world's largest Hyperliquid ETF. "Having now done it a few times, I can say: discussing Hyperliquid with financial advisors is magic," Bitwise CIO Matt Hougan posted on X. "The fact that 99% of fees goes to buying back tokens makes the conversation so easy." Bitwise CEO Hunter Horsley added that Tuesday's trading volume of roughly $22 million meant nearly all of it was net buying. "BHYP is now the largest Hyperliquid ETF in the world," he wrote. "Incredible to see investor interest." Despite the uptick in ETF inflows, HYPE’s price fell nearly 4% in the last 24 hours amid broader market weakness to around $60. Retail sentiment around the decentralized exchange’s token continued to trend in ‘extremely bullish’ territory over the past day, accompanied by ‘extremely high’ levels of chatter. The $19 million single-day haul helped push BHYP to $62.92 million in assets under management (AUM), with the fund now holding over 1 million HYPE tokens. Cumulative net inflows into BHYP stand at $55 million, according to data on SoSoValue. BHYP’s price edged 0.8% lower in morning trade on Wednesday. Retail sentiment around the fund on Stocktwits fell to ‘bearish’ from ‘neutral’ territory over the past day. Chatter stayed at ‘extremely high’ levels. Its closest rival, 21Shares' Hyperliquid ETF (THYP), which launched on Nasdaq on May 12, recorded $44 million in cumulative net inflows. THYP’s price fell nearly 1% in morning trade, but retail sentiment around the fund remained in ‘bullish’ territory over the past day. Together, the two U.S.-listed HYPE spot ETFs have crossed $117 million in combined inflows in just 10 trading sessions, with their largest combined day reaching $25.5 million. BHYP launched on the NYSE on May 15 with a 0.34% sponsor fee, which was waived for the first month on the fund's first $500 million in assets. Bitwise also announced it would allocate 10% of BHYP's management fees to purchasing and holding HYPE on its balance sheet, directly mirroring Hyperliquid's own revenue model. Hyperliquid’s Assistance Fund has directed more than $1.16 billion in trading fees toward open-market HYPE buybacks since launch, according to DefiLlama data. The analytics platform also estimates that roughly 99% of the protocol’s perpetual futures and spot trading revenue flows back into the token repurchase mechanism. Competition in the Hyperliquid ETF market is also beginning to intensify. Grayscale recently filed for its own HYPE ETF. BHYP currently maintains an early advantage after generating the strongest opening-day performance of any U.S.-listed spot altcoin ETF launched in 2026. Detroit's ‘Big Three’ automakers have reportedly received preliminary approval from the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) for industrial bank charters, joining a growing list of financial technology companies, crypto firms, and household-name brands seeking to become banks under the Trump administration. Ford Motor (F), General Motors (GM), and Stellantis (STLA) — the parent company of Chrysler, Jeep, and Ram — each received preliminary deposit-insurance approval from the FDIC for industrial banks, according to a report by The New York Times. Ford’s stock rose nearly 4% in midday trade. Retail sentiment around the company on Stockwits improved to ‘bullish’ from ‘neutral’ over the past day and chatter climbed to ‘high’ from ‘normal’ levels. Meanwhile, GM’s stock jumped nearly 5% but sentiment dropped to ‘neutral’ from the ‘bullish’ zone over the past day. Chatter stayed at ‘high’ levels. STLA’s stock climbed over 4% with retail sentiment trending in ‘extremely bullish’ territory, alongside ‘high’ levels of chatter. The automakers are not alone with the list of companies now seeking or holding bank charters, according to the report. It said that PayPal (PYPL), the payments giant with over 400 million active accounts, has an application under review. So does Affirm (AFRM), the buy now, pay later pioneer that processes billions in consumer credit annually without a banking license of its own. On the crypto side, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) granted conditional national trust bank charters late last year to five crypto ventures, including Ripple Labs, and Fidelity Digital Assets. The charters allow the operators to act as custodians for customers' assets, including cryptocurrency. World Liberty Financial (WLFI), the crypto venture linked to the Trump family, is also among the applicants. Upstart Holdings (UPST), the AI-powered lending platform that underwrote $11 billion in home equity, auto, and personal loans last year, announced in March that it would seek to become a national bank holding company subject to Federal Reserve supervision. Annie Delgado, Upstart's chief risk officer, is the intended chief executive of Upstart Bank if the charter is granted, the report said. Enova (ENVA) and OppFi (OPFI), both of which specialize in short-term consumer lending, are each seeking to obtain charters by acquiring existing nationally chartered banks. For most of these firms, the appeal is straightforward. A banking charter eliminates the need for third-party partner banks to hold customer funds, extend credit, or process payments. An approval would cut costs, increases control, and in the case of a national charter, provide federal pre-emption that allows the holder to operate under a single set of rules across all 50 states rather than navigating a patchwork of state-level regulations. Automakers like Ford, GM, and Stellantis all already operate captive finance subsidiaries that provide auto loans and leases. This includes Ford Motor Credit, GM Financial, and Stellantis Financial Services. An industrial bank charter would give each company more direct control over the funding and management of those loans, potentially lowering their cost of capital and expanding the financial products they can offer customers. The Trump administration has publicly encouraged new entrants into the banking system. Shortly after President Donald Trump began his second term, FDIC leadership called for increased competition in banking. Jonathan Gould, the head of the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, reinforced that position during a Blockchain Association event in December. “New charters ensure a diverse banking sector,” Gould said at the time. “Innovation, competition and fair access should always triumph over regulatory stagnation.” The surge in applications comes during the most active period for new bank charters in more than 15 years. Ethereum's (ETH) "ultrasound money" thesis has effectively broken down, Varys Capital's Head of Venture Capital Tom Dunleavy said on Wednesday, but he thinks the wave of skepticism washing over the network may be the bottom signal itself. Speaking on Scott Melker’s Wolf Of All Streets podcast, Dunleavy zeroed in on recent comments from Bankless founder David Hoffman, who publicly questioned Ethereum's "ultrasound money" identity after years of championing it. Last week, Hoffman posted that he had sold off all of his Ethereum. Dunleavy called Hoffman's change of tone a "classic bottom signal,” the kind of capitulation that tends to show up when one of an asset's loudest believers finally exits the position. In the interview, Melker and Dunleavy both discussed how “Bankless built their entire brand, their funds, their everything around Ethereum.” That said, he was careful to separate the network from the token. Ethereum, the network could still come out fine, he said. The asset is a different conversation and may continue to underperform other crypto narratives for a while, said Dunleavy. Ethereum’s price was down by 0.8% during the past 24 hours, struggling to hold above $2,000. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around ETH shifted to ‘bearish’ from ‘neutral’ zone, while chatter around it remained at ‘high’ levels over the past day. Dunleavy warned that crypto as a whole was running thin on themes worth allocating to. Hedge funds and institutional buyers, he said, have crowded into just a handful of stories, most notably Hyperliquid (HYPE), which is generating real revenue, and Zcash (ZEC), riding the privacy trade. He described Ethereum as in a “ship or die” phase, as competition from newer networks and Wall Street-backed blockchain initiatives intensified. Dunleavy also pointed to a growing “brain drain” at the Ethereum Foundation (EF), noting that several key figures had left this year as the organization increasingly shifted toward privacy-focused initiatives. Despite the criticism of Ethereum's narrative problem, Dunleavy didn't write off the network. He pointed to its dominance in decentralized finance (DeFi) activity, stablecoin issuance, and total value locked, areas where, he argued, the rest of crypto still leans on Ethereum's rails. "If Ethereum fails, crypto fails full stop," he said. “Ethereum has dominated all these metrics consistently for that time period, despite the network activity growing, whatever metric you want to use as a huge pie overall, 5x plus, you know, across chain, so you know, I continue to think if you're betting against Ethereum, you're betting against crypto,” he added. Dunleavy also pushed back hard on the framing around BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust’s (IBIT) $1.29 billion dark pool trade. He called the story "pretty worthless" in the context of Bitcoin (BTC) now trading as a macro asset. According to him, only around $122 million in exchange-traded fund (ETF) redemptions followed the transaction, suggesting that most of the position was privately absorbed rather than triggering broader market stress. title: AbbVie stock holds near highs as new lung cancer data and Q2 2026 growth reshape the outlook - Ad-hoc-news.de
content: AbbVie stock is trading close to its recent high as fresh Q2 2026 revenue growth, stronger Skyrizi and Rinvoq sales, raised full-year guidance, and new lung cancer data presented at WCLC 2026 support the company’s long-term story. AbbVie Inc. (US00287Y1091) stock is trading close to its recent high as investors weigh strong Q2 2026 growth, raised full-year guidance, and new lung cancer data presented at the 2026 World Conference on Lung Cancer as of August 21, 2026. Recent market data show AbbVie shares opening at $265.62 on the latest trading session, a level that sits above a last reported close of $261.07, underscoring modest recent gains and a year-to-date advance of 14.26% as of early July 2026. Per consensus figures compiled in current coverage, the stock carries a rating of Moderate Buy and an average price target of $275.95, leaving a gap of more than $10 between the latest open and the targeted level. For investors, the combination of near-peak trading levels, double-digit revenue growth, and an expanding oncology pipeline makes the AbbVie story more about execution on new therapies than the lingering Humira patent cliff. According to a recent pharmaceutical industry overview on Q2 2026 performance, AbbVie’s net revenue for Q2 2026 rose 10.2% to $17.0 billion, reflecting broad-based growth across its immunology and oncology portfolios for the quarter ended in June 2026. This double-digit increase provides a concrete sign that the company is returning to growth even as Humira faces ongoing biosimilar competition in major markets. The same Q2 2026 review indicates that Skyrizi generated revenue of $5.5 billion in the quarter, while Rinvoq contributed $2.5 billion, with both products delivering year-over-year growth rates of 24.0% and 23.7%, respectively. Together, these two immunology drugs produced $8.03 billion in sales during Q2 2026, more than 10 times the $756 million recorded by Humira, whose revenue declined 36.1% from the prior-year period. This numerical shift illustrates how quickly AbbVie has diversified away from its legacy blockbuster. Historically, Humira dominated AbbVie’s sales mix, but in Q2 2026 Skyrizi and Rinvoq together generated over ten times Humira’s revenue, signaling a decisive transition toward newer therapies that can sustain long-term growth beyond the patent cliff era. Management used the Q2 2026 momentum to raise full-year guidance, lifting projected 2026 net revenue to $67.6 billion. The higher outlook reflects confidence that immunology demand and new indications can carry the business, even as older molecules mature and competitive pressures intensify. The updated full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $67.6 billion represents a step up from prior expectations and underpins the supportive consensus view on AbbVie stock. With Q2 2026 net revenue at $17.0 billion, the implied run-rate suggests that management expects continued solid performance in the back half of the year, helped by expanding use of Skyrizi and Rinvoq and incremental contributions from newer oncology assets. Recent coverage summarizing market data shows AbbVie shares opening at $265.62 on the most recent trading day, while a market quote snapshot lists a last close at $261.07 with a 3.99% single-day gain and a year-to-date performance of 14.26% as of July 2, 2026. At these levels, AbbVie trades below the average analyst price target of $275.95, placing the stock more than 4% under the consensus fair value implied by current models. The spread between the $265.62 open and the $275.95 target highlights that analysts see room for further upside if the company can deliver on its raised guidance and pipeline milestones. In addition, various portfolio filings reported in current data show institutional investors maintaining and adjusting sizable positions in AbbVie, reinforcing the view that the stock remains a core holding for many long-horizon strategies focused on pharma and biotech income and growth. For valuation-focused investors, the key question is whether the strong immunology growth and improving oncology traction can sustain mid-single- to low-double-digit top-line expansion beyond 2026, thereby supporting current price levels and the consensus target. Beyond immunology, AbbVie has been emphasizing its oncology pipeline, and new lung cancer data presented at the 2026 World Conference on Lung Cancer (WCLC 2026) provide important context. According to a company announcement reported in current healthcare coverage, AbbVie showcased new clinical data across multiple lung cancer programs, including non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and small cell lung cancer (SCLC). One detailed report on the WCLC 2026 presentations notes that AbbVie unveiled efficacy and safety updates for investigational therapies such as ABBV-1480, telisotuzumab adizutecan, and ABBV-706. These molecules are being evaluated across various lung cancer settings, with the clinical data focused on response rates, durability, and tolerability in both NSCLC and SCLC populations. The same WCLC 2026 overview explains that AbbVie is pursuing an expanded set of lung cancer trials, positioning these programs as a potential contributor to the company’s future oncology portfolio and longer-term growth profile. The company emphasized that telisotuzumab adizutecan and ABBV-706 remain investigational and are not approved by any health authorities worldwide, underscoring that the lung cancer work is still in the development stage rather than a current commercial driver. In the broader pipeline context, AbbVie has also announced plans for a $10.9 billion acquisition of Apogee Therapeutics to extend its immunology portfolio into dermatology and respiratory disease. When combined with the lung cancer programs, these moves suggest a strategy focused on deepening the company’s presence in immune-mediated and oncology conditions with high unmet need. For investors tracking catalysts, the WCLC 2026 data serve as a forward-looking narrative element: while they do not immediately translate into revenue, they help frame potential future indications and market segments that could complement Skyrizi and Rinvoq as growth drivers later in the decade. Skyrizi, a monoclonal antibody targeting IL-23, and Rinvoq, a JAK inhibitor, have become the cornerstone of AbbVie’s post-Humira immunology strategy. In Q2 2026, their combined $8.03 billion in revenue and growth rates above 20% demonstrate how effectively the company has positioned these drugs across psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis, Crohn’s disease, ulcerative colitis, and other immune-mediated conditions. The Q2 2026 figures show that Skyrizi alone generated $5.5 billion in quarterly revenue, reflecting broad adoption and increasing penetration in existing indications. Rinvoq’s $2.5 billion in revenue, paired with its 23.7% year-over-year growth, signals that AbbVie is successfully leveraging the drug’s label expansion strategy, adding new autoimmune indications over time. On the oncology side, the investigational lung cancer agents highlighted at WCLC 2026 complement AbbVie’s existing hematology and oncology portfolio. ABBV-1480, telisotuzumab adizutecan, and ABBV-706 are being studied in diverse lung cancer cohorts, and the latest data presentations underscore the company’s commitment to building a multi-asset pipeline that could one day rival its immunology franchise in scale. Historically, Humira’s $756 million in Q2 2026 revenue, down 36.1% from the prior-year quarter, reminds investors that legacy product decline remains part of the AbbVie story. Yet the magnitude of the Skyrizi and Rinvoq contribution compared with Humira illustrates that the company has already passed an important inflection point in repositioning its portfolio. Skyrizi serves as a representative product for understanding AbbVie’s current trajectory. Approved for multiple inflammatory indications, Skyrizi is administered as a subcutaneous injection and targets IL-23, a cytokine involved in autoimmune disease pathways. The drug has become widely used in plaque psoriasis, often competing with other biologics that also target IL-23 or related cytokines. In Q2 2026, Skyrizi’s $5.5 billion in revenue underscores its position as one of the largest single products in AbbVie’s lineup. The 24.0% year-over-year growth rate from Q2 2025 to Q2 2026 indicates that the company is still expanding the drug’s reach, both by gaining share in existing indications and by adding new label approvals and geographies. For patients, Skyrizi’s clinical data have highlighted durable skin clearance and symptom relief, while for AbbVie, the drug offers a long-dated patent runway that can support sustainable cash flows. As more real-world data accumulate and physicians gain experience with the therapy, AbbVie is likely to continue emphasizing Skyrizi’s role in differentiated outcomes, especially in difficult-to-treat patient subsets. A prior close of $261.07 as of July 2, 2026, was associated with a single-day gain of 3.99% and a year-to-date advance of 14.26% at that point, indicating solid performance for the stock during 2026. The gap between the $265.62 open and the average price target of $275.95 highlights that current trading levels remain below the consensus fair value derived from recent analyst models. What AbbVie sells, and who pays for it, is the useful way to read its low correlation to the index. AbbVie (ABBV) has gained 4.4% over the last five trading days while the S&P 500 fell 2.0%, and a stock that climbs while the index slips is the kind investors want to chase. The better question is not next week’s price, but whether AbbVie’s returns are genuinely driven by its own story rather than the broader market you already own—and how to hold it accordingly. SKYRIZI And RINVOQ Are Priced With Payers, Not Household Budgets Over five years, ABBV’s correlation to the S&P 500 is 0.22, on a scale where 1.0 is lockstep and 0 is unrelated, so most of what moves this stock is its own story. Look at what the company sells and that stops being surprising. Immunology brought in nearly $8.8 billion of the nearly $17 billion AbbVie sold in the second quarter of 2026, led by SKYRIZI at $5.5 billion and RINVOQ at more than $2.5 billion. These are medicines for chronic disease whose prices management negotiates with payers in contracting season, not at a checkout. The one line that does answer to household budgets is aesthetics, where Allergan Aesthetics promoted Juvederm with buy-one-get-one gift cards in August 2026, and that whole segment was nearly $1.3 billion, about 8% of the quarter. Nor is the stock a second version of a hedge many portfolios already hold: gold’s correlation to ABBV over the same five years is 0.02. ABBV Swings Wider Than The Index: 23.5% Against 17.2% Low correlation is not low volatility. Over the past five years ABBV has delivered an annualized return of 21.5% at an annualized volatility of 23.5%; the S&P 500 returned 12.9% at 17.2%. The stock has paid more and moved wider. The news it moves on is its own: the European Commission approved RINVOQ for non-segmental vitiligo in late July 2026, and the FDA accepted a filing for Botox Cosmetic in masseter muscle prominence in early August 2026. Over the past year, ABBV has traded with even greater independence from the broader market than its five-year baseline suggests. On days the S&P 500 rose, ABBV captured only about 9% of the gain, and on days the index fell, ABBV moved about 26% in the opposite direction, a share of the index’s move rather than of its loss, tending to rise as the market dropped. That is a one-year reading of daily moves, and it can shift. Separately, the business behind the stock is strongly cash-generative: AbbVie converts 28.3% of revenue into free cash flow, against an S&P 500 median of 14.5%. Cash generation of that order is one of the qualities the Trefis High Quality Portfolio favors in its holdings. Hold It For The Independence, Watch The Hidradenitis Suppurativa Data ABBV’s role is a differentiated return engine: over five years it out-returned the index while moving largely on its own, and over the past year it leaned against the market’s down days rather than with them. The swing is wider, not calmer, so this is not a quiet holding on its own; it earns its place beside other stocks that hold up when the index does not. What decides whether that return stream keeps running is the immunology pipeline: management expects 16-week hidradenitis suppurativa data from the RINVOQ and lutikizumab Phase III trials before the end of 2026.
